question: Four modules declare themselves game-neutral. Nothing had ever tried to falsify that.
method: State facts true of a later mainline title and false of Red, and ask the contracts to hold them. No second ROM is required: the question is whether the types can represent a second game, which is the load-bearing part of the transfer claim and is answerable today.
already_neutral: The collection contract holds 251 species across fourteen boxes with namespaced species references that survive a sequel.
battle_matchups reaches type effectiveness through a catalog keyed by type name, so Dark and Steel extend the catalog rather than the contract.

CapturePolicy names no ball. That is correct: when to throw and when to disengage is the neutral rule, and which ball to throw is the adapter's business. An earlier probe scored this as a break; the probe was wrong.

breaks_found_and_repaired.fact: A party member carries a held item.
breaks_found_and_repaired.before: PartyMemberObservation had no field for it.
breaks_found_and_repaired.after: held_item_ref, namespaced, None where the title has none.
breaks_found_and_repaired.why_it_matters: From Gen 2 a held item decides whether a member survives a turn it otherwise would not. A planner that cannot see it is reasoning about a different game than the one it is playing.

breaks_found_and_repaired.fact: Badly poisoned is not the same condition as poisoned.
breaks_found_and_repaired.why_it_matters: Gen 1 carries it as a volatile battle flag and reports plain poison persistently, so Red never emits it. Without it every later adapter has to report something it knows to be false, and toxic damage escalates, so it changes whether a member is safe to keep in.
Breeding is an acquisition route a living Pokedex needs.

breaks_found_and_repaired.fact: One route fields different species by time of day.
breaks_found_and_repaired.before: GrindingArea was identified by area_id alone and summarize_encounters grouped by map id alone.
breaks_found_and_repaired.after: Both carry sorted condition labels; band identity is (area, conditions) and the harvest groups by it.
breaks_found_and_repaired.why_it_matters: This is the worst kind of break because it is silent. Two encounter tables would have merged into a band describing neither, with no error raised -- the only symptom being training that does not converge. It also breaks infrastructure written for this project in the last two days, which is the point: the measured-band pipeline was Red-shaped without anyone noticing.

break_left_open.fact: An egg occupies a party slot and has no level.
break_left_open.status: kept as a strict xfail in tests/test_game_neutrality.py so it stays visible and fails loudly if someone changes the behaviour without updating the record
break_left_open.not_repaired_because: representing eggs touches what a specimen is, not just what fields it carries, and that decision deserves its own design rather than a widened bound

what_did_not_change: Red behaviour. Every new field is optional and defaults to what Red truthfully reports: no held item, no gender, no conditions. Empty conditions is a claim -- 'this title's encounter tables do not vary' -- and it is true of Red. The full local gate went from 2,111 to 2,122 tests with no existing test modified.
verification: Three mutations each turn the suite red: grouping the harvest without conditions, dropping conditions from band identity, and accepting an unnamespaced held item.
why_this_was_worth_doing_before_more_red: The transfer claim is load-bearing for the whole mission and had never been tested. Four of its five assumptions turned out to be wrong, and the most consequential one was silent. Finding that from a second adapter mid-run would have cost far more than finding it from a type.
